scope: news_bot.py: handler-level filter attachment on root logger StreamHandler
regression test: propagated-record path from arbitrary child logger
summary: Round-1 'low' severity finding on propagated-record gap is now fully addressed. The handler-level addFilter call brings root's StreamHandler (the basicConfig-installed one writing to stderr / journald) into the redaction perimeter for ALL records dispatched to it — propagated or originating. This eliminates the residual exposure path from any unaudited child logger.

A02_sensitive_data_exposure.details: All emission paths now covered: (1) records originating on root → root logger-level filter; (2) records originating on httpx-family / anthropic-family → those loggers' logger-level filters; (3) records ORIGINATING ANYWHERE that propagate to root's handlers → root handler-level filter. The only remaining gap would be a child logger that has its OWN handler attached AND propagate=False — that's exotic and not in the SDK we're concerned with.

A09_logging_monitoring_failures.details: Handler-level filter is the canonical Python-logging idiom for catching propagated records. No new attack surface introduced. The fix is iterated only once at import time over root.handlers — no race, no concurrency issue.

findings.finding: Loop iterates root.handlers ONCE at import time — handlers added later (e.g. by tests via caplog, or by an operator hook) won't have the filter. This is acceptable: (a) basicConfig is the only handler installer at our import time; (b) operator-added handlers are explicitly out of our threat model; (c) caplog is test-only and has its own filter chain.
findings.action: no change — within scope for Decision 12

findings.finding: Regression test demonstrates the fix correctly: removing the handler-filter line in news_bot.py causes the test to fail (verified by manual experiment during round-2 review). The test exercises the actual exposure path (StreamHandler → stderr → journald in production).
